title: Beyond KV Reconstruction: Functional Reconstruction for MLA Draft Models in Speculative Decoding
summary: The method replaces direct low-rank MHA/GQA-to-MLA conversion for draft models with a post-conversion calibration procedure that fine-tunes each converted MLA attention module to reproduce the original module's post-output-projection output on calibration hidden states, without verifier logits or supervision. Its cost is an additional per-module optimization stage after conversion, while the converted MLA cache layout and inference graph are preserved, so no extra serving-time memory or latency is introduced. It can fail when acceptance gains do not materialize (26 of 64 cells unchanged, one degraded), when calibration hidden states are unrepresentative of the production workload, or when the reader's stack uses MHA/GQA drafts directly and the MLA conversion step itself is not warranted.
rationale: The technique addresses a real acceptance-rate regression in converted MLA drafts and is feasible on a single GPU, but the gain is inconsistent across configurations, so the reader should validate it on their specific draft-target pair and backend before production adoption.
technique: Functional reconstruction of MLA draft models for speculative decoding

claims.statement: The method replaces direct low-rank MHA/GQA-to-MLA conversion for draft models with a post-conversion calibration procedure that fine-tunes each converted MLA attention module to reproduce the original module's post-output-projection output on calibration hidden states, without verifier logits or supervision. Its cost is an additional per-module optimization stage after conversion, while the converted MLA cache layout and inference graph are preserved, so no extra serving-time memory or latency is introduced. It can fail when acceptance gains do not materialize (26 of 64 cells unchanged, one degraded), when calibration hidden states are unrepresentative of the production workload, or when the reader's stack uses MHA/GQA drafts directly and the MLA conversion step itself is not warranted.

Across 64 matched task cells (four Llama/Qwen draft-target pairs, TransMLA and MHA2MLA converters, HF and vLLM backends, four 200-prompt tasks), functional reconstruction materially improves draft-token acceptance in 37 cells, leaves 26 unchanged within a 0.5-percentage-point tolerance, and decreases one; no aggregate speedup factor is reported.
